Facility Inventory & Condition Assessmen.justification: Comprehensive district-wide inventory including detailed building sizes, ages, portables, classrooms, specialized spaces, and site plans (e.g., Bowers, Bracher, Braly, etc.). Robust condition assessment covers all major systems with lifecycle info and budget projections guiding long-term planning (Page 4, 14-16, 23, 31). Connects condition data to instructional priorities and capital planning.

Enrollment & Capacity Planning.justification: Detailed enrollment projections and capacity utilization by site and classroom with square footage and student counts. Plans link capacity analysis to specific facility actions including phased construction, portables replacement, and adaptive uses (e.g., wellness centers, community use). Explicit strategies for closures, consolidations, and boundary changes are integrated (e.g., Bowers, Braly, Central Park, Montague, Scott Lane).

Educational Alignment.justification: Educational alignment is a core organizing principle with detailed educational specifications for classrooms, specialized spaces (STEM labs, makerspaces, music rooms), and programmatic shifts (e.g., TK, CTE, special education). Facility projects directly respond to educational goals and instructional needs across all campuses (e.g., Don Callejon Arts and Design School, multiple elementary and middle schools).

Outdoor Spaces & Greening.justification: District-wide data on outdoor spaces including square footage of green surfaces, shade coverage, and surface types. Detailed strategies for campus greening such as expanding tree cover, permeable surfaces, outdoor classrooms, rain gardens, and bioswales are included. Outdoor learning and environmental literacy are integrated as part of climate resilience and wellness strategies (e.g., Central Park, Westwood, Peterson Middle School).

Climate Risk & Mitigation.justification: Plan addresses multiple climate impacts with detailed discussion of vulnerabilities (e.g., flood zones at Mayne Elementary) and resilience strategies such as shade structures, stormwater management, and energy resilience. Climate readiness is a theme in assessment and planning but not fully districtwide or across all sites with comprehensive multi-risk assessment (e.g., Mayne Elementary, general sustainability initiatives).

Energy Efficiency & Resilience.justification: Energy resilience and efficiency are core to the plan with data on energy use, strategies for electrification, solar panels, battery storage, and microgrids. References to Title 24, Zero Net Energy goals, and DSA guidance are included. Plans include electrification of HVAC, water heating, kitchens, and renewable integration with resilience to climate disruptions (e.g., district-wide sustainability initiatives, solar panels at multiple sites).

Financial Plan & Capital Strategy.justification: Comprehensive capital strategy with detailed cost estimates, phased prioritization based on safety, equity, program alignment, lifecycle cost, and climate resilience. Multiple funding sources and strategies are outlined including bonds, state programs, developer fees, and alternative financing. Long-term financial sustainability including maintenance, operations, debt capacity, and bond timing are considered (e.g., phased implementation plans across campuses).
